A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effects of pretreatment drugs on cocaine self-administration are not a simple function of drug-induced increases in the reinforcing effects of cocaine, but are also a function of the ability of the pretreatment drugs to affect the discriminative stimulus properties of cocaine.
the effects of pretreatment drugs on cocaine-maintained responding are related to their ability to induce a cocaine-like state.
drugs which produce positive subjective effects (e.g., amphetamine) potentiate reinstatement whereas drugs that produce negative subjective effects (e,g., butorphanol) block reinstatement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of pretreatment drugs on reinstatement of cocaine self-administration are not necessarily the same as the effects on cocaine self-administration.
the effects of pretreatment on the reinstatement of responding may be different from the effects of pretreatments on maintenance of responding.
the effects of a drug on the reinstatement of responding are not always a reliable predictor of its effects on the maintenance of responding.
